lesson.subject: numeracy
lesson.title: Discounts and Sale Prices
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 7, Session 1
lesson.footer: Money and Percentages | Year 5/6 Maths | Session 1

plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Number, Year 6 (VC2M6N09): modelling practical situations involving percentages, such as purchasing items during a sale, with efficient calculation strategies, interpreting results in the situation
plan.shape: example-first with a bar model: the discount is shaded, the sale price is what is left, because confusing the two is the main error
plan.criticalFeature: the discount is the part taken off; the sale price is the part left to pay
decisionPoints: the choice check: sale price of $80 shoes at 25% off
the hinge: a $150 bike at 30% off
plan.anchor: read it, model it, solve it, check it: say what the answer means in the situation

studentTools: Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The fortnight's anchor on the board: read it, model it, solve it, check it

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. A sports shop sale table, bar models, a mistake to fix, and which shop is cheaper.
resources.title: Discounts and Sale Prices
resources.subtitle: Find the discount. Take it off. Check the sale price makes sense.

example.prompt: A $60 cap is 25% off. Find the discount and the sale price.

items.prompt: Find the discount and the sale price of each item.
A $40 jacket is 25% off. Shade the discount and find the sale price.
A $90 tent is 10% off. Shade the discount and find the sale price.
Ella worked out the sale price of a $70 scooter at 20% off. Find her mistake and fix it.
items.answer: $14 is the discount, not the sale price. Sale price = $70 - $14 = $56.

items.prompt: A $200 bike is 40% off. Which is the sale price?

example.prompt: Shop A: $60, 10% off. Shop B: $58, no discount. Cheaper?

items.prompt: Shop A sells runners for $110 with 20% off. Shop B sells them for $95. Which is cheaper, and by how much?
A $45 footy is 'one third off'. Another shop has it at 30% off. Which saves more?
items.answer: One third off saves $15; 30% off saves $13.50. One third off saves more.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. Finding the original price, a discount on a discount, and a sale percentage puzzle, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Sale Detectives
resources.subtitle: Work backwards. Watch out for double discounts.

example.prompt: After 25% off, a game costs $30. Original price?

items.prompt: After 50% off, a hoodie costs $24. What was the original price?
After 20% off, a scooter costs $64. What was the original price?

example.prompt: $100 jacket: 20% off, then a further 10% off the sale price.

items.prompt: A $200 bike is 25% off, then a further 10% off the sale price. Is that the same as 35% off? Show your working.
items.answer: 25% off: $150. 10% of $150 = $15, so $135. 35% off would be $130. Not the same.

example.prompt: A $40 shirt is reduced to $30. What percentage off?

items.prompt: Find the percentage off for each item.
A shop says 'Up to 50% off!'. Write two prices, before and after, that would make this true, and one pair that would make it misleading. Explain.
items.answer: True: $80 to $40 (50% off). Misleading: most items only 10% off, like $50 to $45: 'up to' means only some items get the biggest discount.

resources.label: Supported Worksheet
resources.description: For students who need more guidance: 50% and 10% discounts, a two-step frame, and a hint on every question.
resources.title: Discounts: Step by Step
resources.subtitle: Step 1: the discount. Step 2: take it off.

items.prompt: A $50 hat is 50% off. Discount $___  Sale price $___
A $18 book is 50% off. Discount $___  Sale price $___
A $70 bag is 10% off. Discount $___  Sale price $___
A $120 watch is 10% off. Discount $___  Sale price $___

slides.notes: Session 1 of our money and percentages fortnight: today we work out discounts and sale prices.
Before you start, put boards and markers on every desk; calculators are optional for checking. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

slides.title: Perimeter
prompts: Find the perimeter of the L-shape.

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with area and perimeter.
ASK: What is the perimeter of this L-shape?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 44 m
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> find the missing sides from the opposite sides, then add all six. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The missing sides are 7 and 6, so 12, 4, 7,
6, 5 and 10 make 44 metres. Tick it or fix it.
trap: leaving out the missing sides.
Fix: count the sides, six, and they find the missing ones.
notes.prep: Review of Week 5 area and perimeter (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

slides.title: Area
prompts: A court is 24 m by 15 m. What is its area?

beats: ASK: What is the area of a court 24 metres by 15 metres?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 360 m²
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> split 24 into 20 and 4, multiply each by 15. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 20 times 15 is 300, and 4 times 15 is 60:
360 square metres. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 78, the perimeter.
Fix: say area covers the inside, and they multiply.

slides.title: How many tins?
prompts: A fence is 75 m². A tin of stain covers 20 m². How many tins?

beats: ASK: How many tins of stain are needed?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 4
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> 75 divided by 20, then ask what the remainder means. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 75 divided by 20 is 3, remainder 15,
so we need 4 tins. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 3.
Fix: ask whether 3 tins cover the whole fence, and they round up.

slides.title: Divide with the division bracket: 3 digits

beats: SAY: Now for some short division with the division bracket.
Divide each digit from the left, and carry any remainder across.
ASK: Use the division bracket to solve this one.
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 216
SCAN boards for each digit of the answer.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 216.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: leaving out a zero in the answer when a digit is too small to share.
Fix: ask "How many times does it go?", write 0, and they carry on.
notes.prep: Division fluency: 3 digits, then 4, then 5. Keep the whole block under 6 minutes.

slides.title: Divide with the division bracket: 4 digits

beats: SAY: Now it's 4 digits.
It's the same method, just one more column.
ASK: Use the division bracket to solve this one.
45 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 957
SCAN boards for each digit of the answer.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 957.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: leaving out a zero in the answer when a digit is too small to share.
Fix: ask "How many times does it go?", write 0, and they carry on.

slides.title: Divide with the division bracket: 5 digits

beats: SAY: Now it's 5 digits.
It's the same method, just one more column.
ASK: Use the division bracket to solve this one.
60 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 7 695
SCAN boards for each digit of the answer.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> model the first column together on the board, re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: The answer is 7 695.
Tick it or fix it, and check every step.
trap: leaving out a zero in the answer when a digit is too small to share.
Fix: ask "How many times does it go?", write 0, and they carry on.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to work out discounts and sale prices.
successCriteria: I can find the discount as a percentage of a price.
I can find the sale price by taking the discount off.
I can compare sale prices and explain which is the better deal.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: For the next two weeks we're solving real money problems.
Today it's shopping in a sale.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 the discount is reachable for everyone; SC2 the sale price is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 comparing deals is the stretch.

slides.title: Footy boots on sale
slides.prompt: $120 boots are 25% off. How much do you pay?

beats: POINT to the bar.
SAY: These footy boots normally cost 120 dollars, and they're 25 percent off.
ASK: How much do you pay for the boots in the sale?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $90
SCAN boards for 90.
80%+ -> cold call one student: What did you work out first?
Less -> split the bar into quarters, 30 each, and shade one. Re-ask.
SAY: 25 percent off is 30 dollars off, so you pay 90 dollars.
Some of you wrote 30. That's the discount.
Today we make sure we know which is which.
trap: writing $30.
Fix: ask whether $30 is what you save or what you pay,
and they redo it.
notes.prep: The launch comes after the LI: discount versus sale price, the main confusion. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: The amount taken off the price.
slides.example: A $40 discount on a $160 bike leaves a sale price of $120.

beats: POINT to the word.
SAY: This word is discount. Say it with me: dis-count.
SAY: The discount is the amount taken off the price.
The sale price is what's left, the amount you actually pay.
ASK: A $50 shirt has a $10 discount. What is the sale price?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $40
trap: writing $10.
Fix: ask what you actually pay, and they subtract.
notes.prep: Discount and sale price: name them every time.

beats: MODEL finding the discount.
SAY: These shoes are 80 dollars, 25 percent off.
25 percent is a quarter, so the discount is 20 dollars.
MODEL subtracting.
SAY: The sale price is what's left: 80 take away 20 is 60 dollars.
And 60 is less than 80, so it makes sense.
ASK: A $120 skateboard is 25 percent off. What is the sale price?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $90
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: A quarter of 120 is 30 off, so you pay 90 dollars.
trap: stopping at the discount.
Fix: ask what you pay, and they subtract.
notes.stretch: Find the sale price in one step: 75% of the price.
notes.help: Draw the bar and shade the discount.
notes.prep: Discount first, then sale price, then check: the critical feature. SC1 and SC2.

beats: MODEL 10% first.
SAY: For 30 percent off a 60 dollar jacket,
I find my benchmark: 10 percent is 6 dollars.
MODEL building and subtracting.
SAY: 30 percent is three lots of 6, so 18 dollars off.
60 take away 18 is 42 dollars to pay.
ASK: A $90 tent is 20 percent off. What is the sale price?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $72
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 10 percent is 9, so 20 percent is 18 off: you pay 72 dollars.
trap: subtracting 20 dollars.
Fix: find 10 percent first, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Which is bigger: 30% off $60 or 20% off $90?
notes.help: Write the 10% step first, every time.
notes.prep: Last week's benchmarks, now in a sale. SC2.

slides.title: $80 shoes at 25% off
slides.prompt: What is the sale price? Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: gives the discount, not the sale price

beats: SAY: Think: what do you actually pay?
ASK: What is the sale price of 80 dollar shoes at 25 percent off?
15 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: What is A?
Less -> draw the bar, shade a quarter, and count what's left. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's B, 60 dollars. A is the discount,
and C took off 25 dollars, not 25 percent.
trap: pointing to A.
Fix: ask what you pay at the counter, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point. A: discount for sale price; C: percent as dollars.

slides.title: What is the sale price?
slides.pivot: find the discount on a bar model, then take it off
slides.followUp: cold call one board: What was the discount?

items.say: One third of 36 is 12 off, so you pay 24 dollars.

say: Write each sale price on your board.
trap: writing the discount.
Fix: ask what you pay, and they subtract.
notes.stretch: Write the discount for each one too.
notes.help: Draw a bar and split it into the right number of parts.
notes.prep: Guided practice: each benchmark, then a fraction off. SC2.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
Discount first, then the sale price.
ASK: What is the sale price of a 150 dollar bike at 30 percent off?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $105
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> find 10 percent together, 15, then build 30 percent. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 10 percent is 15, so 30 percent is 45 off:
you pay 105 dollars. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing $45.
Fix: ask what you pay, and they subtract.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work. Anyone writing $45 or $120 starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Work out discounts and sale prices on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: Is that the discount or the sale price?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: writing the discount as the sale price.
Fix: ask what you pay, and they subtract.
notes.stretch: Extension: original prices, double discounts and percentage off.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: 50% and 10% discounts with a two-step frame.
notes.prep: Independent practice: a sale table, bar models, a mistake and comparing shops. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: What is the sale price of a 64 dollar scooter at 25 percent off?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: $48
RECORD who writes the discount or subtracts 25 dollars.
They start tomorrow's check with the teacher.
trap: writing $16 or $39.
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2: a new price at a benchmark discount.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner the difference between a discount and a sale price.

notes.answer: open - listen for discount is taken off; sale price is what you pay
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can work out a sale price?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with $16 on the board matters most.
ASK: What is the difference between a discount and a sale price?
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: discount is taken off; sale price is what you pay
notes.prep: Read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence. Tomorrow: the best buy.
